transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam Ortega (Redwood); Dr. Anika Patel, Carlos Ruiz, Samir Desai, Priya Nair (SilverLinq)

Summary: Quick renewal check-in; customer interested in 12-month contract extension plus EU and APAC activation. They want a small committed uplift up front, with burstable capacity and a private VPC pilot for PHI workloads. Discussed performance expectations, KV cache and batching, security docs, and procurement timing.

Topics: renewal term; provisioning timeline; Private/VPC pilot & KMS; throughput testing and bench; pricing options; procurement deadlines.

[00:00] Maya: All right good afternoon everyone thanks for carving out time. This is Maya from Redwood, Liam our SE is here. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Anika: Morning/afternoon, yes thanks. Busy week but we wanted to lock the renewal mechanics + region activation. We have the board window in July so need clarity on dates.
[00:16] Carlos: Hi, yeah we have a looming quota for EU production by end of July — also apac is lower priority but we'd like a plan there.
[00:23] Liam: Great. Quick agenda: confirm term, sizing options, runbook for EU VPC activation, security checklist, and a plan for throughput testing. Does that sound right?
[00:30] Samir: Yep. We also want to make sure the private bits for PHI workloads are covered — KMS + audit logs.
[00:36] Maya: Absolutely. High level proposal: 12-month extension starting 2027-07-01, two sizing tiers — baseline committed QPS for production and a burst pool. We can stage EU first, run a private VPC pilot for a subset of traffic, then open APAC in Q4.
[00:49] Anika: Can you remind us of the differences between Dedicated and Private again — we get mixed up with the docs.
[00:55] Liam: Sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity in our hosted environment with isolated pools and SLAs; Private (VPC) is customer-managed networking and optional on-prem-like isolation. For PHI we usually recommend VPC + customer KMS; that gives you control of key rotation and HSM if needed. The tradeoff is extra provisioning lead time for peering and firewall rules.
[01:16] Carlos: Lead time — how long? We're targeting EU prod late July.
[01:19] Liam: For a standard VPC pilot we're looking at ~2-3 weeks if network peering and certs are ready. If you need HSM integration or an air-gapped on-prem instance that's longer — 6–8 weeks.
[01:28] Samir: 2-3 weeks ok if we start now. We'll need that runbook — IP ranges, required ports, egress behavior.
[01:33] Maya: Liam will send the provisioning runbook today/tomorrow.

[02:10] Liam: On performance, a couple practical things: your inference pattern (you mentioned lots of short chat-like requests and periodic batch scoring) means we should tune for low-latency tail while still enabling batching for the scoring job. We can suggest batching windows that preserve P99 latency goals. Also prefix KV cache will help for repeated contexts — we saw this reduce token cost in similar health customers.
[02:38] Anika: We had concerns about cold starts and long-tail latency with larger context sizes — will quantization affect quality?
[02:45] Liam: Good point. We recommend a mixed strategy: keep a small pool of warm instances for low-latency paths, and route batch jobs to quantized model variants that are compatible with the runtime. Our Optimize team suggests FP16 or int8 quantization for batch scoring where acceptable. We'll include sample eval numbers.
[02:59] Carlos: Any recent internal benchmarks for EU hw? Last time we saw 180ms med latency for short prompts, is that still realistic?
[03:07] Liam: On the latest gen nodes and with warm instances, 120–150ms median for short prompts is achievable; P99 depends on burst and KV cache hit rate. We'll run your traffic in a throughput test to get numbers.

[05:00] Anika: About security: we need SOC2 Type II evidence, encryption at rest with customer managed keys, and audit log retention for 12 months. Is that supported?
[05:08] Maya: Yes, SOC2 docs are available — we'll share the compliance pack. Customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated depending on config; audit logs can be exported to your S3 with retention settings. We'll include a reference architecture for audit exports.
[05:22] Priya: Procurement question: we need a formal quote and an amendment to the existing contract showing the 12-month term and the committed units. Do you have a template for the purchase order?
[05:30] Maya: Yes, I'll attach a redlined amendment and two price points — conservative and peak. We'll call out committed units, burst pool, and optional add-ons like extended observability retention.

[07:10] Samir: Networking nuance — do you support static egress IPs for API callbacks? We need that for our firewall rules.
[07:17] Liam: We can provide an IP allowlist for peered VPCs and static NAT ranges for certain deployments. For hosted Dedicated there's a set of egress ranges we publish; for VPC peering the traffic stays within the peer. We'll put exact CIDRs in the runbook.

[09:45] Carlos: Pricing — can you give us a sense of unit economics? At our current usage the token cost is a big line item. We want to understand the tradeoffs if we move more to batch scoring (lower cost) vs chat (higher cost).
[09:55] Maya: Yep. We'll show per-token costs across model variants and an expected monthly spend under both profiles. Also show how caching and batching change the effective cost per inference. We'll include a short ROI slide.

[12:00] Anika: For the throughput test we're planning to run EU with a subset of prompts containing PHI. Are there masking/rewrite best practices?
[12:08] Liam: Two approaches: mask/replace PHI before sending, or run in VPC with KMS + RBAC and strict audit logs. For evaluation we can do a synthetic trace where PHI is tokenized/masked so you avoid sending production PHI in test. But for final staging you can do VPC pilot.

[15:30] Maya: Timeline proposal:
- Week of 2027-06-06: finalize PO and sizing.
- Week of 2027-06-13: throughput test in EU (we run with your traces).
- 2027-06-20 to 2027-06-30: provision VPC, peering and cert validations.
- 2027-07-01: contract start / EU go-live (soft launch).
- Q4 2027: APAC staged activation.

[16:10] Priya: That July 1 start is tight but doable if we get the quote by Friday and we push approvals.
[16:20] Maya: We'll aim to get pricing by Thursday 2027-06-03.

[19:00] Anika: One technical ask: when you do the throughput test can you surface per-token cost and KV cache hit rates so we can tune context windows?
[19:08] Liam: Yes. We'll instrument the test to export token counts, latency percentiles, and cache hit metrics. That will help pick model/quantization choices.

[22:40] Carlos: Any vendor lock-in concerns if we go for Private? We need to be able to fall back to a smaller on-prem model in case of service disruption.
[22:48] Liam: We support model variants and automatic fallback policies — we can configure routing that fails over to a smaller quantized model or an on-prem inference endpoint. We'll document the failover steps and time-to-failover.

[26:00] Samir: Regarding observability — we need tracing hooks into our existing APM. Is there an integration?
[26:06] Liam: Yes, Redwood Console supports trace exports and per-route logs; we have a lightweight SDK that forwards traces to common APMs. We'll include an integration example for DataDog/NewRelic.

[31:10] Anika: Is there a recommended rollback policy for canary deploys? We sometimes see model regressions after a rollout.
[31:18] Liam: Canary 10% for 24 hours with automatic quality checks (we'll run evals on a prompt set). If quality drops beyond threshold, automatic rollback and routing to previous pinned variant. Also we can configure gradual ramp.

[36:40] Carlos: Does the quote include price breaks if we commit annual min consumption? We'd likely sign a larger commitment if price per token drops materially.
[36:48] Maya: Yes. Two-tier pricing: baseline and committed/volume tiers. We'll show both and highlight breakpoints for the 12-month term. Also note dedicated GPU reservation offers further savings.

[40:00] Priya: Any open security reviews? We might need an info-sec session with your security team — compatibility with our DLP workflows.
[40:06] Maya: We can set a 45-60m security deep-dive next week; I'll coordinate with Product Security. We'll include an example DLP architecture.

[44:20] Anika: OK final clarifying question: If we sign the extension, can we reserve an additional 20% burst capacity for peak loads with an automatic billing trigger?
[44:27] Liam: Yes, we support a burst pool that bills for actual usage above committed. There's also an option for a pre-purchased burst credit pack for predictable cost. We'll include that option in the quote.

[47:00] Maya: Quick recap of action items: pricing by 2027-06-03, runbook by 2027-06-04, throughput test week of 2027-06-13, procurement decision by 2027-06-08.
[47:12] Priya: Sounds good, we'll try to accelerate approvals.
[47:20] Samir: I'll start prepping network team for peering.

[50:00] Carlos: Thanks all, good coverage. We'll follow up after we review the quote.
[50:05] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and files after the call.
[50:12] Anika: Thanks, bye.
[50:15] End of meeting
